rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Dispersion quantifies the roam. **Range** is instant but crude; **mean deviation** averages |xᵢ − x̄| (minimised at the median); **variance** σ² = Σxᵢ²/n − x̄² squares the deviations — analytic but with squared units — and **σ = √σ²** restores them (NEB 2024: mean 25, σ ≈ 9.41 for the 10-mark set; NEB 2023: variance of 1…10 is 385/10 − 5.5² = **8.25**). Adding a constant leaves σ unchanged; scaling scales it.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - σ² = (1/n)Σ(xᵢ − x̄)² = (1/n)Σxᵢ² − x̄²; σ = √σ² - C.V. = (σ/x̄) × 100% - Pearson skewness: (x̄ − mode)/σ or 3(x̄ − median)/σ - Σi² = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6; variance of first n naturals = (n²−1)/12

rows.text: ❌ treat "Measure of dispersion: standard deviation" as one blob → ✅ split into: measure of dispersion: standard deviation, variance, coefficient of variation.  ·  ❌ state the rule without its limit → ✅ note when it applies / stops applying.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "sigma^2 = (1/n) sum xi^2 - (mean)^2; CV = (sigma/mean) x 100; Pearson skewness = (mean - mode)/sigma."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Mean of squares minus square of mean*** — sigma^2 = sum(xi^2)/n - xbar^2: the one identity that turns variance into two running sums, no deviation table required.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Measuring the Spread Central tendency says where data sits; **dispersion** says how widely it roams. The theorem set: **range**, **mean deviation**, **variance and standard deviation** (with the computational identity σ² = E(x²) − [E(x)]²), the **coefficient of variation**, and **Karl Pearson's skewness** coefficients.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Range and mean deviation - **Range** = max − min — crude but instant. - **Mean deviation** = (1/n)Σ|xᵢ − x̄| — average distance from the mean; about the median it is minimised (a theorem: the median minimises Σ|xᵢ − a|). ### 2.2 Variance and standard deviation - **Variance:** σ² = (1/n)Σ(xᵢ − x̄)² — mean squared deviation.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: SD via the identity: mean of squares minus square of mean. First n naturals: sigma^2 = (n^2 - 1)/12. Lower CV wins consistency. Skewness sign: mean - mode.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): The marks obtained by 10 students in a test are 12, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25, 28, 30, 35 and 45. Calculate (i) the mean, and (ii) the standard deviation. (4m)** — **(i) Mean:** x̄ = Σxᵢ/n = (12 + 15 + 18 + 20 + 22 + 25 + 28 + 30 + 35 + 45)/10 = 250/10 = **25**.…  ·  **NEB 2023 (verified PYQ): The variance of the first 10 natural numbers is: (a) 8.25 (b) 9.25 (c) 10.25 (d) 11.25 (1m)** — Data: 1, 2, …, 10 with mean (10+1)/2 = 5.5. **Sum of squares formula:** Σxᵢ² = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 = (10)(11)(21)/6 = **385**.…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Variance squares to stay analytic, then takes a root to speak in data units; dividing by the mean (C.V.) makes spread comparable across different scales.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Range = max - min. Mean deviation = (1/n) sum |xi - xbar|; minimised about the median. Variance: sigma^2 = (1/n) sum (xi - xbar)^2 = (1/n) sum xi^2 - xbar^2 (computational identity). Standard deviation sigma = sqrt(variance), same units as data.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The C.V. is why a ±5 error on a 1000 g weighing is excellent and on a 10 g weighing is a disaster: relative, not absolute, spread tells the story.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): Two machines fill packets with means 500 g and 505 g and standard deviations 4 g and 6 g respectively. Which is more consistent?** — **Coefficient of variation** is the fair comparator: C.V.₁ = (4/500) × 100 = **0.8%**; C.V.₂ = (6/505) × 100 ≈ **1.19%**. The **lower C.V.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Variance** | Mean squared deviation from the mean | σ² = Σxᵢ²/n − x̄² | | **Standard deviation** | √variance — typical distance from the mean | same units as data | | **Coefficient of variation** | Relative spread: σ/x̄ × 100% | unit-free comparison | | **Skewness** | Asymmetry of the…  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why squares for variance - Absolute values are awkward analytically; squares are differentiable and additive. The price: units get squared — the √ in σ restores them. ### 4.2 The computational identity at work - σ² = Σxᵢ²/n − x̄² lets you compute variance from running sums — no deviation table needed, and it is the identity examiners test.…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **Dispersion measures compared** | Measure | Uses | Robust to outliers? | |---|---|---| | Range | extremes only | no | | Mean deviation | absolute distances | somewhat | | Standard deviation | squared distances | no (squares amplify) | | C.V. | relative spread | no |

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **NEB 2023 (verified PYQ): The variance of the first 10 natural numbers is: (1m MCQ)** — First 10 naturals: 1…10, mean 5.5. Σxᵢ² = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 = 10·11·21/6 = 385. Variance = 385/10 − (5.5)² = 38.5 − 30.25 = **8.25 → option (a)**. The formula shortcut n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 turns this into a 30-second question.  ·  **NEB 2022 (verified PYQ): If P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.5, P(A∩B) = 0.3, then P(A∪B) is: (1m)** — **Addition law:** P(A∪B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A∩B) = 0.6 + 0.5 − 0.3 = **0.8 → option (a)**.
